title: Daily Market Digest: Tech Sell-off Drags Indices Lower Amid AI Spending Scrutiny
subtitle: October 30, 2026 Close

items.headline: Tech Sell-off Dominates Friday Trading as AI Spending Concerns Mount
items.summary: U.S. equities closed lower on Friday, October 30, with technology stocks leading the decline following disappointing earnings reports and intensified scrutiny over the high cost of AI infrastructure investment. While the Dow managed a more modest dip, the S&P 500 and particularly the Nasdaq felt significant pressure. Defensive sectors like Health Care and Real Estate showed resilience amidst the broader market weakness.

items.headline: Regeneron Surges on Strong Q3 Earnings
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals climbed significantly after reporting a robust third-quarter earnings beat and raising its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Veralto Beats Earnings, Raises Guidance
items.summary: Industrial technology company Veralto surged after exceeding Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations and subsequently raising its guidance.

items.headline: Mondelez Rises on Strong Q3 Performance
items.summary: Mondelez International posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, leading to a notable increase in its stock price.

items.headline: Intel Plunges on Weak Guidance and AI Costs
items.summary: Intel shares plummeted after the semiconductor giant issued disappointing third-quarter results and a weak outlook, fueling concerns over AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Reddit Falls Following Big Tech Earnings
items.summary: Reddit experienced a significant drop, becoming a casualty of negative investor reaction to after-hours earnings reports from other major technology companies.

items.headline: Amazon Slides on Weaker Profit and AI Spending Outlook
items.summary: Amazon's stock fell as the company reported a weaker profit for the quarter than anticipated and signaled continued heavy investment in AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Tech and Communication Services Lag as Defensives Lead
items.summary: The Information Technology and Communication Services sectors were among the day's worst performers, declining by 1.2% and 1.9% respectively, as concerns over AI spending continued to weigh on investor sentiment. In contrast, defensive sectors such as Health Care (+2.4%), Real Estate (+2.2%), Consumer Staples (+1.38%), and Energy (+1.30%) showed relative strength.

items.headline: Economic Data Shows Slower Business Activity, Rising Inflation
items.summary: The Chicago Business Barometer fell to 55.3 in October from 58.8 the previous month, indicating a slower pace of business activity expansion in the Chicago area. Meanwhile, third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate, notably boosted by an AI-led investment boom with non-residential fixed investment growing 9.4%. However, September's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation jumped to a 6.1% annual rate, pushing the year-over-year rate to 3.6%, signaling persistent inflationary pressures. Core PCE inflation also rose.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports Drive Individual Stock Movements
items.summary: Beyond Intel and Amazon's notable declines, several major companies reported earnings today. ExxonMobil ($XOM) and Chevron ($CVX) both rose following better-than-expected third-quarter profits, driven by strong refining margins. AbbVie ($ABBV) announced strong Q3 results with diluted EPS increasing over 100%. Cboe Global Markets ($CBOE) also reported strong third-quarter financial results, with diluted EPS up 43%. General Dynamics ($GD) reported solid Q3 operating earnings and revenue growth across all segments.

items.headline: Oil Prices Rise, Treasury Yields Ease, Crypto Markets Hit by Breach
items.summary: Oil prices gained ground today, with Brent crude rising 2% to $113.04 per barrel amidst global energy market disruptions. Concurrently, Treasury yields eased as investors sought safer assets amid market uncertainty. In cryptocurrency markets, a reported $6.3 billion security breach at Binance, one of the world's largest digital asset exchanges, led to significant selling pressure.
